evidence: OOT Gini 0.340 vs Lending Club sub-grade 0.411 (difference -0.071, 95% CI -0.081 to -0.061). Fails the success criterion.
recommendation: Not to be used as the primary decision score. Can be used alongside the existing grade (+0.017 Gini when combined).

evidence: Observed / predicted 1.19 (mean PD 3.40% vs default rate 4.04%); 8 of 10 deciles fail the binomial test; Hosmer-Lemeshow p < 0.001.
recommendation: Recalibrate the intercept to the latest observed default rate and add a margin of conservatism before any PD use (pricing, provisions, capital).

evidence: Observed / predicted 1.05 for LightGBM monotone; 4 of 10 deciles fail the binomial test (deciles 6-8). CatBoost monotone is the best calibrated (0.99).
recommendation: Recalibrate (e.g. intercept shift on the most recent matured cohort) before PD use; monitor the observed / predicted ratio quarterly.

finding: Calibration differs before and from 2016; boosting's lead depends on the 2016 fields
evidence: Scorecard observed / predicted is 0.89 on test loans issued before 2016 and 1.17 on 2016 loans: the model is fitted on a mixture of periods with and without these fields, while every OOT loan has them. Ablation: without the 14 fields, observed/predicted on 2016 test loans rises from 1.02 to 1.17, and on OOT from 1.05 to 1.19.
recommendation: Re-estimate (or at least recalibrate) on 2016+ loans once enough matured history is available; document the design choice.

finding: Target is a reconstruction, not observed 90+ dpd
evidence: Default month is derived from instalments paid (96.3% agreement with the date method on matured loans). Cured delinquencies are invisible. Results are robust to removing debt settlements (Gini changes by at most 0.003).
recommendation: Accepted for development on public data; in production, validate against actual delinquency history.

finding: Partial, data-derived constraints; main driver loan_amnt is unconstrained
evidence: Constraints cover 21 of 78 features, with directions derived from data. loan_amnt is the 2nd most important feature by SHAP, but was excluded from the scorecard (IV 0.015, non-monotonic) and is unconstrained in boosting.
recommendation: Document the business rationale of its effect and check its shape (partial dependence) before use; include it in adverse-action reason codes.

evidence: No protected characteristics in the data. By state: adverse impact ratio >= 0.95 (passes the four-fifths rule), but calibration varies from 0.75 to 1.22 observed / predicted.
recommendation: Before deployment, run a fair-lending analysis with inferred protected classes (e.g. BISG); monitor state-level calibration.

evidence: LightGBM tuning and early stopping used the same holdout (Gini 0.458 there vs 0.443 on test); CatBoost was not tuned. Boosting in-sample Gini 0.52-0.59 vs test 0.44.
recommendation: Use a separate tuning holdout in the next development cycle; tune CatBoost before final champion selection.

evidence: 2013-2017 contains no recession (PD is not through-the-cycle); only funded loans are observed (no reject inference); joint applications excluded.
recommendation: State in the model documentation; apply a downturn adjustment if the PD is used for capital.

evidence: Developer and validator are the same person.
recommendation: Obtain a review by an independent party.

evidence: Success criteria changed during development; recalibration method and the 0.9-1.1 tolerance were chosen after seeing OOT. Monotone preference was set before OOT on explainability, but not as a written rule.
recommendation: Pre-register decisions and confirm on an untouched matured cohort.
status: Open; early 2018 check supports ranking, LightGBM recalibration not confirmed

evidence: Reasons for the grade's strength, verification risk and differences in default rates by issue year are unproven. On test, removing verification_status and initial_list_status lowers Gini by about 0.003 across four seeds; Verified share rises from 18% in grade A to 59% in grade G on train. This fits a lender effect but does not prove it.
recommendation: Test them or label them as hypotheses.

finding: Target horizon is shorter than the product
evidence: Matured 2013-2015 test loans default at 3.2% in 12 months and 14.2% over their life. Same-period lifetime Gini favours LightGBM (0.368 vs 0.340), but a model fitted on 2013-2014 ranks 2015 below the sub-grade: lifetime Gini 0.349 vs 0.357.
recommendation: Limit use to early-default ranking; do not claim lifetime superiority; repeat when 2017 matures.
